Subject: Suspicious auth failures seen — request for IR plan and artifacts

Hi Jordan,

We started seeing elevated authentication failures and a spike in 401 responses for several of our production flows this morning (around 08:40 PST). Our security team flagged what looks like repeated token refresh errors and unusual IPs in the auth logs. We need Redwood's incident response plan and any immediate telemetry you can share (S3 access logs, auth audit trail, deployment timeline) so we can correlate with our side.

Could you: 
- Confirm whether Redwood observed anomalous auth errors around 08:30–09:00 PST
- Share the IR contact and an expected ETA for initial artifacts
- Provide a secure upload location or next steps for evidence transfer

This is time-sensitive for our regulators; please prioritize.

Thanks,
Emily Zhang

Emily / team — final postmortem and evidence packet attached. Summary pasted below.

On Fri, Nov 13, 2026 at 11:30 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Emily, Jordan — I’m taking point. Thanks for escalating, Emily. Quick summary of what we can and will deliver...

Redwood Postmortem (summary):
- Incident window: 08:33–09:12 PST
- Root cause: an orchestrator rollout unintentionally disabled a token refresh receiver on a small subset of inference workers. That caused cascade refresh failures in ~0.6% of customer requests routed through a specific regional pool.
- Impact: elevated 401 counts and transient errors for calls proxied via that pool; latency spike for a small subset of requests. No customer data exfiltration detected.
- Containment: automatic fallback to healthy pool at 08:45 PST (routing rule engaged), manual rollback of the rollout at 09:02 PST.
- Remediation (completed): fix to rollout gating to prevent disabling refresh receiver; added automated smoke test that validates refresh flow on new cohorts; updated runbook to surface token-refresh telemetry within 2 minutes.
- Follow-ups: scheduled SIGC AIQ mapping update, expanded log retention for auth traces related to rollouts, and a short tabletop drill next quarter.

Artifacts provided (links/attachments):
- redacted_s3_access_logs.csv (sample subset for 08:30–09:15 PST)
- timeline_snapshot_11-13-2026.json (machine-readable timeline)
- ir_postmortem_20261113.md (full postmortem, remediation owner list)

Access and sharing: the artifacts are available via the Redwood secure evidence folder (Drive link below) with a pre-signed S3 URL for direct download. We redacted other customers and removed full user-Agent strings per your request.

If Orchard wants a live review call to walk through the timeline, we can schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow morning.

Thanks — and apologies again for the disruption.

— Karthik Iyer
Senior Applied ML Engineer — Redwood Inference
